svg.text: Private AI Services 3.0, the bare minimum: 15 steps on one host to a model endpoint
My lab, October 2026: vSphere 9.1.1 on a single host, no NSX, no VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) Automation. One box is one step, the coloured line says where it happens.
ONE ESX HOST: vCenter, Supervisor, Private AI Services (PAIS), Harbor, the Kubernetes cluster and every model run on this machine
Supermicro H12SSL-NT · AMD EPYC 7513, 32 cores · 512 GB memory · 2 × 4 TB NVMe as local datastores · 2 × 10 GbE onboard · one RTX A5000, 24 GB
ESX and vCenter, cluster with DRS and HA,
switch with three port groups, storage policy
Foundation Load Balancer, one control plane VM
VM classes for control plane and endpoints
PRIVATE AI SERVICES (PAIS): Model Runtime only
registry token from the portal, added as
a container registry on the Supervisor
register, then install on the Supervisor
Model Runtime only, CPU only, local user.
PAIS builds its own VKS cluster
one patch for apiTokens, one annotation
for the name, then generate a token
service name to a remote model, key in a Secret
lab and PoC only: CA, registry, project
registry entry with the CA on the Supervisor,
weights as OCI artifacts in Harbor
card to passthrough on the host, VM class,
vGPU instead: several endpoints share one card,
needs an NVIDIA licence, see part 4a
one YAML object: model, engine, VM class.
PAIS adds the worker node and pulls the model
the route points the service name to the local
model: one URL, one token, no client changes
AI GATEWAY OF PAIS: what application teams get for remote and local models
one OpenAI-compatible URL, one API token, one service name per model
Steps 1 to 9 need no GPU and no registry of your own. Steps 10 to 12 are done once, steps 14 and 15 repeat for every model.
A change to the registry credentials or the CA bundle replaces the control plane of the PAIS cluster. In the lab that took 10 to 15 minutes each time.
